assembly_instructions: 1. Press the four rubber feet into the underside of the lower frame corners and place the lower front, rear, left, and right 2020 extrusions on a flat bench. 2. Bolt the lower extrusion rectangle together, add the four corner gusset plates, and square the base before tightening. 3. Fasten the four vertical 2020 posts to the lower frame and attach the upper front, rear, left, and right extrusions to form the cube frame. 4. Install the Z guide rods, lower bearing blocks, top bearings, lead screws, motor coupler, and synchronizing belt so both screws rotate together. 5. Bolt the bed carriage strips to the Z nuts and guide-rod bearing blocks, then install the four leveling screws, compression springs, and thumb knobs. 6. Fit the cutaway heated aluminum bed, silicone heater pad, and glass build-plate strips on the leveling screws, leaving the center open in this instructional model to expose the under-bed hardware. 7. Mount the left and right Y linear rails on the top side extrusions and bolt the Y carriage blocks to the moving X gantry rail. 8. Attach the X linear guide to the gantry, install the X carriage bearing, carriage plate, belt clamps, and local strain-relief clamp. 9. Mount the two CoreXY stepper motors, motor drive pulleys, rear idlers, front idlers, and pulley shafts, then route and tension the front, rear, side, crossed, and short carriage-side belt spans around the carriage. 10. Assemble the hotend on the carriage by stacking the extruder body, Bowden coupler, PTFE collar, heat sink, fan, heater block, heater cartridge, thermistor, and downward brass nozzle. 11. Attach the side spool bracket, paired side plates, diagonal braces, spindle, spool hub, flanges, and filament coil, then route the filament through the guide eyelet and segmented PTFE Bowden tube into the coupler. 12. Install the PSU, controller board, terminal block, display, segmented cable chain, hotend heater wires, and bed heater leads, then verify frame square, Z bed motion, nozzle clearance, belt tension, cable bend radius, and electrical continuity before calibration.

metadata.info: Open-frame desktop CoreXY-style FDM printer with a vertically moving heated bed, side spool holder, Bowden-fed hotend, and exposed motion components for assembly legibility.
facts: Nominal build volume represented as 235 mm x 235 mm x 250 mm, a common desktop FDM size class.
Frame members are modeled as 20 mm square aluminum extrusions, scaled to 3.4 m scene width for visibility while preserving relative proportions.
Filament path is sized for 1.75 mm filament and terminates at a 0.4 mm brass nozzle.
The build plate is shown as cutaway strips equivalent to a 235 mm x 235 mm x 4-6 mm glass sheet so the heater and leveling hardware remain visible.
Spool is represented as a 200 mm diameter by 70 mm wide 1 kg PLA spool, scaled to the scene.
Z screws are represented as paired 8 mm lead screws with anti-backlash nuts supporting the bed carriage.
XY belt spans represent 6 mm GT2 timing belts commonly used on desktop printers.
PSU is labeled as a 24 V, 350 W supply typical for bed-heated FDM machines.
NEMA-17 stepper motors are represented as 42 mm square bodies, scaled consistently with the frame.
Linear guide rails are shown as narrow steel bars with distinct carriage blocks so the X and Y motion axes can be traced visually.
sources: Prusa Research, Original Prusa i3 MK3S+ handbook and technical specifications for 1.75 mm filament, 0.4 mm nozzle, and 250 mm class Z travel.
Voron Design V2.4 assembly manual for CoreXY belt routing, 2020 extrusion frame construction, and stationary gantry layout.
Creality Ender-3 S1 specifications for 220-235 mm class heated bed and 24 V desktop printer electronics.
Gates Industrial, PowerGrip GT2 synchronous belt design data for small-pitch timing belt geometry.
